newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end off, play on OTCs, electronic.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end off, play on OTCs, electronic.

text.p: Singapore shares ended weaker on Tuesday as selling pressure by institutions overshadowed retail interest in electronic and over-the-counter (OTC) stocks.
"Institutions were mostly selling but there was good speculative play by retail investors," said a dealer, adding that their focus was on OTCs and electronic counters.
Dealers said retail investors were also taking a second look at stocks launched in last year's initial public offers such as Labroy Marine.
After trading to a low of 2,209.50, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index ended at 2,215.52, down 16.88 points.

Electronic counter, SM Summit Holdings, led the actives with over 14.8 million shares. It rose Singapore $0.055 (US$0.04) to end at S$0.715. Dealers said the stock, listed last year, was being re-rated together with other electronic shares.

Recent activity in Malaysian counters subsided on fears that Japanese funds were unloading Malaysian shares. Investment firm KLI Holdings was heavily traded, with volume of over 9.0 million shares on rumours of a share placement, a share swap and a possible infrastructure contract.
Singapore Press Foreign rose S$0.50 to S$27.50 while UOB Foreign fell S$0.50 to S$16.00.
